name: Miniamin
overview: Miniamin was a male member of the tribe of Levi and is noted as an ancestor of Piltai. He belonged to the priestly lineage descending from Aaron, indicating his family's role in the religious leadership of Israel. His descendants are recognized among the priests, emphasizing their service in the temple.
namesAndTitles: The name Miniamin means 'from the right, good, fortune,' reflecting positive attributes. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Miniamin is explicitly identified as a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, situating him within the Levitical priesthood. He is also the father of Piltai, establishing a direct familial line important for priestly heritage. Scripture does not record other family relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Miniamin's significance lies in his role as a forefather within the Levitical priesthood, specifically as an ancestor of Piltai, a priest mentioned in the post-exilic period. His connection to Aaron highlights the continuity of priestly service through his lineage. This underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant with the tribe of Levi and the preservation of priestly duties across generations.
